flashcard_questions.q: What is the principal focus of a lens?
flashcard_questions.a: The point where parallel rays converge, or appear to diverge from, after the lens.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the focal length of a lens?
flashcard_questions.a: The distance from the centre of the lens to the principal focus.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a convex lens affect parallel rays of light?
flashcard_questions.a: It refracts them inwards so they converge at the principal focus.

flashcard_questions.q: What image does a convex lens form when the object is beyond the focal point?
flashcard_questions.a: A real, inverted image that can be captured on a screen.

flashcard_questions.q: What image does a convex lens form when the object is closer than the focal point?
flashcard_questions.a: A virtual, upright, magnified image, as in a magnifying glass.

flashcard_questions.q: What type of image does a concave lens always produce?
flashcard_questions.a: A virtual, upright image that is smaller than the object.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation is used to calculate magnification?
Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
What is the approximate wavelength of violet light?
Why does a red shirt look black under blue light?
flashcard_questions.a: There is no red light for it to reflect, and it absorbs the blue light.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a colour filter do to light passing through it?
flashcard_questions.a: It absorbs certain wavelengths and transmits others.

flashcard_questions.q: What is specular reflection of light?
flashcard_questions.a: Reflection from a smooth surface where all rays travel in the same direction.

flashcard_questions.q: What is diffuse reflection of light?
flashcard_questions.a: Reflection from a rough surface where rays scatter in many directions.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a perfect black body?
flashcard_questions.a: An object that absorbs all of the radiation that falls on it.

flashcard_questions.q: When is an object in thermal equilibrium?
flashcard_questions.a: When it absorbs radiation at the same rate as it emits radiation.
